[HACKTOBERFEST]  Help Wanted: Contribute New Problems to Our Question Bank!
# 🧩 Contribute Competitive Programming Problems

## 📘 Description
We are looking to **expand our collection of competitive programming problems** to provide more practice opportunities for our users.  
This is a great opportunity for anyone to contribute — **no matter your experience level!**

Your task is simple: **add new problems** to our database file following the given format.

---

## 🚀 How to Contribute

### 1. 🔍 Find a Problem
Find an interesting programming problem from any competitive programming platform (like **Codeforces**, **LeetCode**, **AtCoder**, **GeeksforGeeks**, etc.) that you'd like to add.

---

### 2. 📂 Navigate to the File
All our problems are stored in:

src/constants/problems.tsx


---

### 3. 🧱 Understand the Format

Problems are stored in a `ProblemsMap` object, grouped by **difficulty rating** (e.g., `"800"`, `"1200"`, etc.).  
Each problem entry must follow the `Problem` interface:

```ts
export interface Problem {
  id: string;             // Unique ID, e.g., "p800-2"
  title: string;          // Problem title, e.g., "A. Halloumi Boxes"
  description: string;    // The problem statement.
  input_format: string;   // Description of the input.
  output_format: string;  // Description of the output.
  test_case: string;      // A sample test case with multiple inputs.
  answer: string;         // The corresponding answers for the test case.
  solved: boolean;        // Should always be `false`.
}
```
## 4. 🧩 Add Your Problem

Choose the difficulty level (e.g., "800", "1000", etc.).
If it doesn’t exist, create a new key for it in the object.

Copy the template below and fill in your problem details.

🧠 Problem Template
```
{
  "id": "p<difficulty>-<unique_number>",
  "title": "<Problem Title>",
  "description": "<Problem Description>",
  "input_format": "<Input Format Description>",
  "output_format": "<Output Format Description>",
  "test_case": "<Sample Test Cases>",
  "answer": "<Corresponding Answers>",
  "solved": false
}
```
## 5. 🧾 Example

If you’re adding a problem with a difficulty of 1000, your file should look like this:

// src/constants/problems.tsx

```
export const problem: ProblemsMap = {
  '800': [
    // ... existing 800-level problems
  ],
  '1000': [
    {
      "id": "p1000-1",
      "title": "B. Example Problem",
      "description": "This is an example problem description.",
      "input_format": "The first line contains...",
      "output_format": "For each test case, print...",
      "test_case": "2\n5\n1 2 3 4 5",
      "answer": "YES\nNO",
      "solved": false
    }
    // You can add more problems here
  ]
  // ... other difficulties
};
```
## 6. 🪄 Create a Pull Request

Once you’ve added your problems:

Commit your changes with a descriptive message (e.g., Added new problem at difficulty 1000).

Submit a Pull Request (PR).

Our team will review it and merge it once it meets the format.

### 💡 Notes

-> Please ensure unique IDs for each problem (p<difficulty>-<number>).
-> Single PR would only be accepted if it contributes atleast 5 problems
-> Keep problem statements concise but clear.
-> Do not modify existing problems unless fixing typos or formatting.
-> Multiple problem additions in a single PR are welcome!

Thank you for helping us make CanonForces a better platform for everyone! 💙
Your contributions make a real impact on our community.

[HACKTOBERFEST]  Help Wanted: Contribute New Problems to Our Question Bank!
# 🧩 Contribute Competitive Programming Problems

## 📘 Description
We are looking to **expand our collection of competitive programming problems** to provide more practice opportunities for our users.  
This is a great opportunity for anyone to contribute — **no matter your experience level!**

Your task is simple: **add new problems** to our database file following the given format.

---

## 🚀 How to Contribute

### 1. 🔍 Find a Problem
Find an interesting programming problem from any competitive programming platform (like **Codeforces**, **LeetCode**, **AtCoder**, **GeeksforGeeks**, etc.) that you'd like to add.

---

### 2. 📂 Navigate to the File
All our problems are stored in:

src/constants/problems.tsx


---

### 3. 🧱 Understand the Format

Problems are stored in a `ProblemsMap` object, grouped by **difficulty rating** (e.g., `"800"`, `"1200"`, etc.).  
Each problem entry must follow the `Problem` interface:

```ts
export interface Problem {
  id: string;             // Unique ID, e.g., "p800-2"
  title: string;          // Problem title, e.g., "A. Halloumi Boxes"
  description: string;    // The problem statement.
  input_format: string;   // Description of the input.
  output_format: string;  // Description of the output.
  test_case: string;      // A sample test case with multiple inputs.
  answer: string;         // The corresponding answers for the test case.
  solved: boolean;        // Should always be `false`.
}
```
## 4. 🧩 Add Your Problem

Choose the difficulty level (e.g., "800", "1000", etc.).
If it doesn’t exist, create a new key for it in the object.

Copy the template below and fill in your problem details.

🧠 Problem Template
```
{
  "id": "p<difficulty>-<unique_number>",
  "title": "<Problem Title>",
  "description": "<Problem Description>",
  "input_format": "<Input Format Description>",
  "output_format": "<Output Format Description>",
  "test_case": "<Sample Test Cases>",
  "answer": "<Corresponding Answers>",
  "solved": false
}
```
## 5. 🧾 Example

If you’re adding a problem with a difficulty of 1000, your file should look like this:

// src/constants/problems.tsx

```
export const problem: ProblemsMap = {
  '800': [
    // ... existing 800-level problems
  ],
  '1000': [
    {
      "id": "p1000-1",
      "title": "B. Example Problem",
      "description": "This is an example problem description.",
      "input_format": "The first line contains...",
      "output_format": "For each test case, print...",
      "test_case": "2\n5\n1 2 3 4 5",
      "answer": "YES\nNO",
      "solved": false
    }
    // You can add more problems here
  ]
  // ... other difficulties
};
```
## 6. 🪄 Create a Pull Request

Once you’ve added your problems:

Commit your changes with a descriptive message (e.g., Added new problem at difficulty 1000).

Submit a Pull Request (PR).

Our team will review it and merge it once it meets the format.

### 💡 Notes

-> Please ensure unique IDs for each problem (p<difficulty>-<number>).
-> Single PR would only be accepted if it contributes atleast 5 problems
-> Keep problem statements concise but clear.
-> Do not modify existing problems unless fixing typos or formatting.
-> Multiple problem additions in a single PR are welcome!

Thank you for helping us make CanonForces a better platform for everyone! 💙
Your contributions make a real impact on our community.


---

[HACKTOBERFEST]  Help Wanted: Contribute New Problems to Our Question Bank!
# 🧩 Contribute Competitive Programming Problems

## 📘 Description
We are looking to **expand our collection of competitive programming problems** to provide more practice opportunities for our users.  
This is a great opportunity for anyone to contribute — **no matter your experience level!**

Your task is simple: **add new problems** to our database file following the given format.

---

## 🚀 How to Contribute

### 1. 🔍 Find a Problem
Find an interesting programming problem from any competitive programming platform (like **Codeforces**, **LeetCode**, **AtCoder**, **GeeksforGeeks**, etc.) that you'd like to add.

---

### 2. 📂 Navigate to the File
All our problems are stored in:

src/constants/problems.tsx


---

### 3. 🧱 Understand the Format

Problems are stored in a `ProblemsMap` object, grouped by **difficulty rating** (e.g., `"800"`, `"1200"`, etc.).  
Each problem entry must follow the `Problem` interface:

```ts
export interface Problem {
  id: string;             // Unique ID, e.g., "p800-2"
  title: string;          // Problem title, e.g., "A. Halloumi Boxes"
  description: string;    // The problem statement.
  input_format: string;   // Description of the input.
  output_format: string;  // Description of the output.
  test_case: string;      // A sample test case with multiple inputs.
  answer: string;         // The corresponding answers for the test case.
  solved: boolean;        // Should always be `false`.
}
```
## 4. 🧩 Add Your Problem

Choose the difficulty level (e.g., "800", "1000", etc.).
If it doesn’t exist, create a new key for it in the object.

Copy the template below and fill in your problem details.

🧠 Problem Template
```
{
  "id": "p<difficulty>-<unique_number>",
  "title": "<Problem Title>",
  "description": "<Problem Description>",
  "input_format": "<Input Format Description>",
  "output_format": "<Output Format Description>",
  "test_case": "<Sample Test Cases>",
  "answer": "<Corresponding Answers>",
  "solved": false
}
```
## 5. 🧾 Example

If you’re adding a problem with a difficulty of 1000, your file should look like this:

// src/constants/problems.tsx

```
export const problem: ProblemsMap = {
  '800': [
    // ... existing 800-level problems
  ],
  '1000': [
    {
      "id": "p1000-1",
      "title": "B. Example Problem",
      "description": "This is an example problem description.",
      "input_format": "The first line contains...",
      "output_format": "For each test case, print...",
      "test_case": "2\n5\n1 2 3 4 5",
      "answer": "YES\nNO",
      "solved": false
    }
    // You can add more problems here
  ]
  // ... other difficulties
};
```
## 6. 🪄 Create a Pull Request

Once you’ve added your problems:

Commit your changes with a descriptive message (e.g., Added new problem at difficulty 1000).

Submit a Pull Request (PR).

Our team will review it and merge it once it meets the format.

### 💡 Notes

-> Please ensure unique IDs for each problem (p<difficulty>-<number>).
-> Single PR would only be accepted if it contributes atleast 5 problems
-> Keep problem statements concise but clear.
-> Do not modify existing problems unless fixing typos or formatting.
-> Multiple problem additions in a single PR are welcome!

Thank you for helping us make CanonForces a better platform for everyone! 💙
Your contributions make a real impact on our community.


---

issue_2_text: [HACKTOBERFEST] Feat: Implement real-time user search page ## 📝 Overview The search bar in the main header is currently non-functional. This issue proposes implementing a dedicated, full-screen search experience to allow users to find other people on the platform in real-time. Clicking the search bar will navigate to a new `/search` route, which will provide an immersive interface focused solely on searching and displaying user results. ## ✨ Acceptance Criteria ### 1. Navigation and Page Layout - [ ] Clicking the main search bar in the header should navigate the user to a new `/search` page. - [ ] The `/search` page should display a prominent search input bar at the top, which is focused automatically upon page load. - [ ] The main content area below the search bar should initially be blank or display a simple prompt like "Search for users by name or username." ### 2. Real-Time Search Functionality - [ ] As the user types into the search input, the application should query the user database in real-time. - [ ] To optimize performance, the search query should be **debounced** (e.g., trigger after the user stops typing for 300-500ms). - [ ] The search should match against both the user's **full name** and their **username**. ### 3. Displaying Results - [ ] Search results should be displayed as a list of user cards below the search bar as they are fetched. - [ ] Each result item should be a reusable component that displays the user's: - Profile Picture - Full Name - Username (e.g., `@handle`) - [ ] If a search query yields no results, a clear message like "No users found for '[query]'" should be displayed. - [ ] Clicking on any user card in the search results should navigate to that user's public profile page (e.g., `/user/:userId`). ## 🎨 UI/UX Considerations - A loading indicator (e.g., a spinner or skeleton loader) should be visible while the search query is in progress. - The transition to the `/search` page should be smooth. - The user result cards should be visually consistent with the existing `UserSuggestionCard` component. ## 🛠️ Technical Notes - A new page component will need to be created at `pages/search.tsx`. - Implement a **debouncing** custom hook or use a library like `use-debounce` to manage the search input and prevent excessive API calls. - A new Firestore query function is needed. Since Firestore has limitations with partial text search, the query might need to check for a `startsWith` condition on the username or name fields. For a more robust solution, a third-party search service like **Algolia** could be considered in the future.

-   [ ] Remove the "Messages" link and icon from the primary sidebar.
-   [ ] Add a new "Contests" link and icon to the sidebar.

issue_2_text: [HACKTOBERFEST] Bug: Contest Timestamps are Not Converted to Local Time (IST) # [Bug] Contest Timestamps are Not Converted to Local Time ### Description The "Upcoming Contests" component appears to be displaying all contest times in a single, default timezone (likely UTC) instead of converting them to the user's local timezone. This causes the displayed times to be incorrect for users in different parts of the world. ### Current Behavior - The contest times are displayed in a static, non-local timezone. - For a user in Indian Standard Time (IST), the displayed times are incorrect and do not match their local time. - **Example:** A contest listed with an afternoon time in the UI may actually be scheduled for the evening in the user's local timezone, but the UI does not reflect this conversion. ### Expected Behavior - The application should detect the user's local timezone from their browser or system settings. - All contest timestamps should be automatically converted from their source timezone to the user's local timezone before being displayed. - **Example:** The time shown for each contest should accurately reflect when the event will start in the user's current location. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Set your computer's timezone to one that is different from the server's default (e.g., IST, EST, etc.). 2. Navigate to the "Upcoming Contests" page. 3. Observe that the times displayed do not match the correct local start times for the events. ### Possible Solution This can likely be solved on the front-end by using a JavaScript library like `date-fns`, `moment.js`, or the native `Intl.DateTimeFormat` API to parse the incoming date string and format it for the user's locale.

[HACKTOBERFEST]  Help Wanted: Contribute New Problems to Our Question Bank!
# 🧩 Contribute Competitive Programming Problems

## 📘 Description
We are looking to **expand our collection of competitive programming problems** to provide more practice opportunities for our users.  
This is a great opportunity for anyone to contribute — **no matter your experience level!**

Your task is simple: **add new problems** to our database file following the given format.

---

## 🚀 How to Contribute

### 1. 🔍 Find a Problem
Find an interesting programming problem from any competitive programming platform (like **Codeforces**, **LeetCode**, **AtCoder**, **GeeksforGeeks**, etc.) that you'd like to add.

---

### 2. 📂 Navigate to the File
All our problems are stored in:

src/constants/problems.tsx


---

### 3. 🧱 Understand the Format

Problems are stored in a `ProblemsMap` object, grouped by **difficulty rating** (e.g., `"800"`, `"1200"`, etc.).  
Each problem entry must follow the `Problem` interface:

```ts
export interface Problem {
  id: string;             // Unique ID, e.g., "p800-2"
  title: string;          // Problem title, e.g., "A. Halloumi Boxes"
  description: string;    // The problem statement.
  input_format: string;   // Description of the input.
  output_format: string;  // Description of the output.
  test_case: string;      // A sample test case with multiple inputs.
  answer: string;         // The corresponding answers for the test case.
  solved: boolean;        // Should always be `false`.
}
```
## 4. 🧩 Add Your Problem

Choose the difficulty level (e.g., "800", "1000", etc.).
If it doesn’t exist, create a new key for it in the object.

Copy the template below and fill in your problem details.

🧠 Problem Template
```
{
  "id": "p<difficulty>-<unique_number>",
  "title": "<Problem Title>",
  "description": "<Problem Description>",
  "input_format": "<Input Format Description>",
  "output_format": "<Output Format Description>",
  "test_case": "<Sample Test Cases>",
  "answer": "<Corresponding Answers>",
  "solved": false
}
```
## 5. 🧾 Example

If you’re adding a problem with a difficulty of 1000, your file should look like this:

// src/constants/problems.tsx

```
export const problem: ProblemsMap = {
  '800': [
    // ... existing 800-level problems
  ],
  '1000': [
    {
      "id": "p1000-1",
      "title": "B. Example Problem",
      "description": "This is an example problem description.",
      "input_format": "The first line contains...",
      "output_format": "For each test case, print...",
      "test_case": "2\n5\n1 2 3 4 5",
      "answer": "YES\nNO",
      "solved": false
    }
    // You can add more problems here
  ]
  // ... other difficulties
};
```
## 6. 🪄 Create a Pull Request

Once you’ve added your problems:

Commit your changes with a descriptive message (e.g., Added new problem at difficulty 1000).

Submit a Pull Request (PR).

Our team will review it and merge it once it meets the format.

### 💡 Notes

-> Please ensure unique IDs for each problem (p<difficulty>-<number>).
-> Single PR would only be accepted if it contributes atleast 5 problems
-> Keep problem statements concise but clear.
-> Do not modify existing problems unless fixing typos or formatting.
-> Multiple problem additions in a single PR are welcome!

Thank you for helping us make CanonForces a better platform for everyone! 💙
Your contributions make a real impact on our community.


---

[HACKTOBERFEST] fix(UI): Properly render inline code backticks in problem descriptions ## 📝 Overview The problem descriptions fetched from our database use markdown-style backticks (`) to denote variables and inline code snippets ). Currently, these backticks are being rendered as plain text in the UI instead of being parsed into styled code elements. This negatively affects readability and gives an unpolished look to the "Problem of the Day" component and the main problem-solving page. This issue proposes implementing a dedicated, full-screen search experience to allow users to find other people on the platform in real-time. Observe that the times displayed do not match the correct local start times for the events. ### Possible Solution This can likely be solved on the front-end by using a JavaScript library like `date-fns`, `moment.js`, or the native `Intl.DateTimeFormat` API to parse the incoming date string and format it for the user's locale.

[HACKTOBERFEST]  Help Wanted: Contribute New Problems to Our Question Bank!
# 🧩 Contribute Competitive Programming Problems

## 📘 Description
We are looking to **expand our collection of competitive programming problems** to provide more practice opportunities for our users.  
This is a great opportunity for anyone to contribute — **no matter your experience level!**

Your task is simple: **add new problems** to our database file following the given format.

---

## 🚀 How to Contribute

### 1. 🔍 Find a Problem
Find an interesting programming problem from any competitive programming platform (like **Codeforces**, **LeetCode**, **AtCoder**, **GeeksforGeeks**, etc.) that you'd like to add.

---

### 2. 📂 Navigate to the File
All our problems are stored in:

src/constants/problems.tsx


---

### 3. 🧱 Understand the Format

Problems are stored in a `ProblemsMap` object, grouped by **difficulty rating** (e.g., `"800"`, `"1200"`, etc.).  
Each problem entry must follow the `Problem` interface:

```ts
export interface Problem {
  id: string;             // Unique ID, e.g., "p800-2"
  title: string;          // Problem title, e.g., "A. Halloumi Boxes"
  description: string;    // The problem statement.
  input_format: string;   // Description of the input.
  output_format: string;  // Description of the output.
  test_case: string;      // A sample test case with multiple inputs.
  answer: string;         // The corresponding answers for the test case.
  solved: boolean;        // Should always be `false`.
}
```
## 4. 🧩 Add Your Problem

Choose the difficulty level (e.g., "800", "1000", etc.).
If it doesn’t exist, create a new key for it in the object.

Copy the template below and fill in your problem details.

🧠 Problem Template
```
{
  "id": "p<difficulty>-<unique_number>",
  "title": "<Problem Title>",
  "description": "<Problem Description>",
  "input_format": "<Input Format Description>",
  "output_format": "<Output Format Description>",
  "test_case": "<Sample Test Cases>",
  "answer": "<Corresponding Answers>",
  "solved": false
}
```
## 5. 🧾 Example

If you’re adding a problem with a difficulty of 1000, your file should look like this:

// src/constants/problems.tsx

```
export const problem: ProblemsMap = {
  '800': [
    // ... existing 800-level problems
  ],
  '1000': [
    {
      "id": "p1000-1",
      "title": "B. Example Problem",
      "description": "This is an example problem description.",
      "input_format": "The first line contains...",
      "output_format": "For each test case, print...",
      "test_case": "2\n5\n1 2 3 4 5",
      "answer": "YES\nNO",
      "solved": false
    }
    // You can add more problems here
  ]
  // ... other difficulties
};
```
## 6. 🪄 Create a Pull Request

Once you’ve added your problems:

Commit your changes with a descriptive message (e.g., Added new problem at difficulty 1000).

Submit a Pull Request (PR).

Our team will review it and merge it once it meets the format.

### 💡 Notes

-> Please ensure unique IDs for each problem (p<difficulty>-<number>).
-> Single PR would only be accepted if it contributes atleast 5 problems
-> Keep problem statements concise but clear.
-> Do not modify existing problems unless fixing typos or formatting.
-> Multiple problem additions in a single PR are welcome!

Thank you for helping us make CanonForces a better platform for everyone! 💙
Your contributions make a real impact on our community.


---

This issue proposes implementing a dedicated, full-screen search experience to allow users to find other people on the platform in real-time. Clicking the search bar will navigate to a new `/search` route, which will provide an immersive interface focused solely on searching and displaying user results. ## ✨ Acceptance Criteria ### 1. Displaying Results - [ ] Search results should be displayed as a list of user cards below the search bar as they are fetched. - [ ] Each result item should be a reusable component that displays the user's: - Profile Picture - Full Name - Username (e.g., `@handle`) - [ ] If a search query yields no results, a clear message like "No users found for '[query]'" should be displayed. - [ ] Clicking on any user card in the search results should navigate to that user's public profile page (e.g., `/user/:userId`). ## 🎨 UI/UX Considerations - A loading indicator (e.g., a spinner or skeleton loader) should be visible while the search query is in progress. - The transition to the `/search` page should be smooth. - The user result cards should be visually consistent with the existing `UserSuggestionCard` component. ## 🛠️ Technical Notes - A new page component will need to be created at `pages/search.tsx`. - Implement a **debouncing** custom hook or use a library like `use-debounce` to manage the search input and prevent excessive API calls. - A new Firestore query function is needed. Since Firestore has limitations with partial text search, the query might need to check for a `startsWith` condition on the username or name fields. For a more robust solution, a third-party search service like **Algolia** could be considered in the future.

This causes the displayed times to be incorrect for users in different parts of the world. ### Current Behavior - The contest times are displayed in a static, non-local timezone. - For a user in Indian Standard Time (IST), the displayed times are incorrect and do not match their local time. - **Example:** A contest listed with an afternoon time in the UI may actually be scheduled for the evening in the user's local timezone, but the UI does not reflect this conversion. ### Expected Behavior - The application should detect the user's local timezone from their browser or system settings. - All contest timestamps should be automatically converted from their source timezone to the user's local timezone before being displayed. - **Example:** The time shown for each contest should accurately reflect when the event will start in the user's current location. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Set your computer's timezone to one that is different from the server's default (e.g., IST, EST, etc.). 2. Navigate to the "Upcoming Contests" page. 3. Observe that the times displayed do not match the correct local start times for the events. ### Possible Solution This can likely be solved on the front-end by using a JavaScript library like `date-fns`, `moment.js`, or the native `Intl.DateTimeFormat` API to parse the incoming date string and format it for the user's locale.

Currently, POTD is fetched correctly, but there’s no system to maintain or visualize who solved each day’s challenge. (For now you can just add checkbox beside question which if user checks then will consider he has solved the POTD) This feature aims to: - Store daily solvers for each POTD - Display the list of solvers dynamically on the POTD page - Lay the groundwork for future features like streaks, coins, and badges --- ### 🧠 Expected Flow 1. On the POTD page, fetch and render the list of solvers (with real-time updates using `onSnapshot`). 3. Optional: Sort solvers by timestamp so early solvers appear first (like a mini leaderboard). --- ### 🔧 Tech Stack - **Frontend:** Next.js + Firebase SDK - **Database:** Firestore - **Realtime Updates:** Firestore onSnapshot --- ### 💡 Example UI Enhancement Under the existing “First Solvers Today” section: ```tsx {solvers.map((solver, i) => (
  • 🏅 {i + 1}. {solver.username}
    • ))}

## 📝 Feature Request: Add PR & Issue Templates with Review Workflow

### 📌 Context
We already have templates for Issues and PRs, but they can be improved to:
- Ensure contributors provide **complete context** (what/why/how).
- Encourage **screenshots/demos** for UI changes.
- Standardize **review requests** (tagging maintainers / CODEOWNERS).
- Save time during reviews by making PRs & issues self-explanatory.

### 🔧 Suggested Improvements

#### 📝 Pull Request Template
- Add a **"Why this change?"** section → helps reviewers understand intent.
- Add **Screenshots / Loom video** section (if applicable).
- Add **Checklist** (tests, docs, linting, review request).
- Add **Reviewers mention section**.

### 🚀 What to Add
1. **Pull Request Template**
   - Clear checklist for contributors (what/why/changes/tests/docs).
   - Section to link issues, screenshots (if UI change), and reviewers.
   - Example PR template content:
     ```markdown
     ## 📌 Related Issue
     Closes #ISSUE_ID

     ## ✨ Changes Introduced
     - [ ] Summary of changes

     ## 🖼️ Screenshots (if applicable)
     _Before / After_

     ## ✅ Checklist
     - [ ] Tested locally
     - [ ] Added/Updated docs
     - [ ] Added tests (if required)
     - [ ] Requested review from maintainers

     ## 👥 Reviewers
     @mention reviewers here
     ```

[HACKTOBERFEST] Style: Profile Page UI Redesign
# 🎨 UI/UX Improvement: Profile Page Redesign

## 📌 Description
The current **Profile Page UI** feels empty and unbalanced. Important user information (solved problems, followers, ratings) does not stand out, and there is excessive whitespace.  

### Current Issues:
- Stats (Solved, Followers, Following) are plain text and not visually highlighted.  
- Codeforces info is shown in a basic list format → lacks hierarchy.  
- Right-side illustration feels disconnected and does not add value.  
- Too much blank space makes the profile look unfinished.  

## ✅ Expected Improvements
- Enhance **profile header**: show cover/banner, profile picture, name, username more prominently.  
- Display **stats (Solved, Followers, Following, Ratings)** in styled cards or badges.  
- Redesign **Codeforces data** (rank, rating, max rating) → maybe with progress bars or colored badges matching Codeforces tiers.  
- Better alignment of right-side illustration, or replace it with something more functional (e.g., activity chart, recent submissions).  
- Add subtle **background styling** or separators to avoid the "empty" feel.  

## 📂 References / Inspiration
- LeetCode profile design  
- Codeforces profile sections  
- GitHub profile layout  

## 🧩 Impact
- Makes the **profile page more engaging**  
- Highlights achievements and encourages user motivation  
- Improves overall **UI/UX consistency** across Canonforces

# 📝 Feature Request: Upcoming Contests Section

## 📌 Overview
Add a new **section on the Home Page** (can be placed anywhere as a separate block) to display **upcoming programming contests** from popular platforms like:
- Codeforces  
- LeetCode  
- CodeChef  
- AtCoder  

## 🎯 Feature Details
- A **dedicated section** that shows the next few contests with:
  - Contest **name**
  - **Date & time**
  - **Duration**
  - A **direct link** to participate/register
- Auto-fetch contests using APIs (e.g., [Kontests API](https://kontests.net/) or platform-specific APIs).
- Keep the UI **minimal & readable** (e.g., card layout / table view).

- Developers often miss contests → this keeps them **informed at a glance**.  
- Saves time instead of checking each platform individually.  
- Adds more **value** to the home page by mixing practice with real-world contests.  

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Shows upcoming contests (at least from Codeforces & LeetCode).  
- [ ] Each contest entry has a link to the original contest page.  
- [ ] Data should auto-refresh (on reload / scheduled fetch).  

## 📂 Additional Notes
- Can later extend to other platforms (CodeChef, AtCoder, HackerRank).  
- Future idea: Allow **reminders/notifications** for contests.

- End of quiz → **score summary** (correct/incorrect, accuracy, time spent).

- Fullscreen mode = better **focus** during quizzes.
- AI-generated or dynamic questions = **infinite variety** of practice.

- [ ] Timer runs automatically (global OR per-question).

This issue proposes implementing a dedicated, full-screen search experience to allow users to find other people on the platform in real-time. Clicking the search bar will navigate to a new `/search` route, which will provide an immersive interface focused solely on searching and displaying user results. ## ✨ Acceptance Criteria ### 1. Navigation and Page Layout - [ ] Clicking the main search bar in the header should navigate the user to a new `/search` page. - [ ] The `/search` page should display a prominent search input bar at the top, which is focused automatically upon page load. - [ ] The main content area below the search bar should initially be blank or display a simple prompt like "Search for users by name or username." ### 2. Real-Time Search Functionality - [ ] As the user types into the search input, the application should query the user database in real-time. - [ ] To optimize performance, the search query should be **debounced** (e.g., trigger after the user stops typing for 300-500ms). - [ ] The search should match against both the user's **full name** and their **username**. ### 3. Displaying Results - [ ] Search results should be displayed as a list of user cards below the search bar as they are fetched. - [ ] Each result item should be a reusable component that displays the user's: - Profile Picture - Full Name - Username (e.g., `@handle`) - [ ] If a search query yields no results, a clear message like "No users found for '[query]'" should be displayed. - [ ] Clicking on any user card in the search results should navigate to that user's public profile page (e.g., `/user/:userId`). ## 🎨 UI/UX Considerations - A loading indicator (e.g., a spinner or skeleton loader) should be visible while the search query is in progress. - The transition to the `/search` page should be smooth. - The user result cards should be visually consistent with the existing `UserSuggestionCard` component. ## 🛠️ Technical Notes - A new page component will need to be created at `pages/search.tsx`. - Implement a **debouncing** custom hook or use a library like `use-debounce` to manage the search input and prevent excessive API calls. - A new Firestore query function is needed. Since Firestore has limitations with partial text search, the query might need to check for a `startsWith` condition on the username or name fields. For a more robust solution, a third-party search service like **Algolia** could be considered in the future.

Observe that the times displayed do not match the correct local start times for the events. ### Possible Solution This can likely be solved on the front-end by using a JavaScript library like `date-fns`, `moment.js`, or the native `Intl.DateTimeFormat` API to parse the incoming date string and format it for the user's locale.

issue_1_text: [HACKTOBERFEST] Feat: Implement real-time user search page ## 📝 Overview The search bar in the main header is currently non-functional. This issue proposes implementing a dedicated, full-screen search experience to allow users to find other people on the platform in real-time. Clicking the search bar will navigate to a new `/search` route, which will provide an immersive interface focused solely on searching and displaying user results. ## ✨ Acceptance Criteria ### 1. Navigation and Page Layout - [ ] Clicking the main search bar in the header should navigate the user to a new `/search` page. - [ ] The `/search` page should display a prominent search input bar at the top, which is focused automatically upon page load. - [ ] The main content area below the search bar should initially be blank or display a simple prompt like "Search for users by name or username." ### 2. Real-Time Search Functionality - [ ] As the user types into the search input, the application should query the user database in real-time. - [ ] To optimize performance, the search query should be **debounced** (e.g., trigger after the user stops typing for 300-500ms). - [ ] The search should match against both the user's **full name** and their **username**. ### 3. Displaying Results - [ ] Search results should be displayed as a list of user cards below the search bar as they are fetched. - [ ] Each result item should be a reusable component that displays the user's: - Profile Picture - Full Name - Username (e.g., `@handle`) - [ ] If a search query yields no results, a clear message like "No users found for '[query]'" should be displayed. - [ ] Clicking on any user card in the search results should navigate to that user's public profile page (e.g., `/user/:userId`). ## 🎨 UI/UX Considerations - A loading indicator (e.g., a spinner or skeleton loader) should be visible while the search query is in progress. - The transition to the `/search` page should be smooth. - The user result cards should be visually consistent with the existing `UserSuggestionCard` component. ## 🛠️ Technical Notes - A new page component will need to be created at `pages/search.tsx`. - Implement a **debouncing** custom hook or use a library like `use-debounce` to manage the search input and prevent excessive API calls. - A new Firestore query function is needed. Since Firestore has limitations with partial text search, the query might need to check for a `startsWith` condition on the username or name fields. For a more robust solution, a third-party search service like **Algolia** could be considered in the future.

This issue proposes replacing the "Messages" section in the main sidebar with a more functional and relevant "Contests" section. The goal is to centralize all contest-related features into a single, dedicated page, improving user navigation and adding value by including contest solutions.

issue_2_text: [HACKTOBERFEST] Bug: Contest Timestamps are Not Converted to Local Time (IST) # [Bug] Contest Timestamps are Not Converted to Local Time ### Description The "Upcoming Contests" component appears to be displaying all contest times in a single, default timezone (likely UTC) instead of converting them to the user's local timezone. This causes the displayed times to be incorrect for users in different parts of the world. ### Current Behavior - The contest times are displayed in a static, non-local timezone. - For a user in Indian Standard Time (IST), the displayed times are incorrect and do not match their local time. - **Example:** A contest listed with an afternoon time in the UI may actually be scheduled for the evening in the user's local timezone, but the UI does not reflect this conversion. ### Expected Behavior - The application should detect the user's local timezone from their browser or system settings. - All contest timestamps should be automatically converted from their source timezone to the user's local timezone before being displayed. - **Example:** The time shown for each contest should accurately reflect when the event will start in the user's current location. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Set your computer's timezone to one that is different from the server's default (e.g., IST, EST, etc.). 2. Navigate to the "Upcoming Contests" page. 3. Observe that the times displayed do not match the correct local start times for the events. ### Possible Solution This can likely be solved on the front-end by using a JavaScript library like `date-fns`, `moment.js`, or the native `Intl.DateTimeFormat` API to parse the incoming date string and format it for the user's locale.

issue_2_text: [HACKTOBERFEST] Bug: Contest Timestamps are Not Converted to Local Time (IST) # [Bug] Contest Timestamps are Not Converted to Local Time ### Description The "Upcoming Contests" component appears to be displaying all contest times in a single, default timezone (likely UTC) instead of converting them to the user's local timezone. This causes the displayed times to be incorrect for users in different parts of the world. ### Current Behavior - The contest times are displayed in a static, non-local timezone. - For a user in Indian Standard Time (IST), the displayed times are incorrect and do not match their local time. - **Example:** A contest listed with an afternoon time in the UI may actually be scheduled for the evening in the user's local timezone, but the UI does not reflect this conversion. ### Expected Behavior - The application should detect the user's local timezone from their browser or system settings. - All contest timestamps should be automatically converted from their source timezone to the user's local timezone before being displayed. - **Example:** The time shown for each contest should accurately reflect when the event will start in the user's current location. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Set your computer's timezone to one that is different from the server's default (e.g., IST, EST, etc.). 2. Navigate to the "Upcoming Contests" page. 3. Observe that the times displayed do not match the correct local start times for the events. ### Possible Solution This can likely be solved on the front-end by using a JavaScript library like `date-fns`, `moment.js`, or the native `Intl.DateTimeFormat` API to parse the incoming date string and format it for the user's locale.

issue_2_text: [HACKTOBERFEST] Bug: Contest Timestamps are Not Converted to Local Time (IST) # [Bug] Contest Timestamps are Not Converted to Local Time ### Description The "Upcoming Contests" component appears to be displaying all contest times in a single, default timezone (likely UTC) instead of converting them to the user's local timezone. This causes the displayed times to be incorrect for users in different parts of the world. ### Current Behavior - The contest times are displayed in a static, non-local timezone. - For a user in Indian Standard Time (IST), the displayed times are incorrect and do not match their local time. - **Example:** A contest listed with an afternoon time in the UI may actually be scheduled for the evening in the user's local timezone, but the UI does not reflect this conversion. ### Expected Behavior - The application should detect the user's local timezone from their browser or system settings. - All contest timestamps should be automatically converted from their source timezone to the user's local timezone before being displayed. - **Example:** The time shown for each contest should accurately reflect when the event will start in the user's current location. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Set your computer's timezone to one that is different from the server's default (e.g., IST, EST, etc.). 2. Navigate to the "Upcoming Contests" page. 3. Observe that the times displayed do not match the correct local start times for the events. ### Possible Solution This can likely be solved on the front-end by using a JavaScript library like `date-fns`, `moment.js`, or the native `Intl.DateTimeFormat` API to parse the incoming date string and format it for the user's locale.

issue_1_text: [HACKTOBERFEST] Bug: Contest Timestamps are Not Converted to Local Time (IST) # [Bug] Contest Timestamps are Not Converted to Local Time ### Description The "Upcoming Contests" component appears to be displaying all contest times in a single, default timezone (likely UTC) instead of converting them to the user's local timezone. This causes the displayed times to be incorrect for users in different parts of the world. ### Current Behavior - The contest times are displayed in a static, non-local timezone. - For a user in Indian Standard Time (IST), the displayed times are incorrect and do not match their local time. - **Example:** A contest listed with an afternoon time in the UI may actually be scheduled for the evening in the user's local timezone, but the UI does not reflect this conversion. ### Expected Behavior - The application should detect the user's local timezone from their browser or system settings. - All contest timestamps should be automatically converted from their source timezone to the user's local timezone before being displayed. - **Example:** The time shown for each contest should accurately reflect when the event will start in the user's current location. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Set your computer's timezone to one that is different from the server's default (e.g., IST, EST, etc.). 2. Navigate to the "Upcoming Contests" page. 3. Observe that the times displayed do not match the correct local start times for the events. ### Possible Solution This can likely be solved on the front-end by using a JavaScript library like `date-fns`, `moment.js`, or the native `Intl.DateTimeFormat` API to parse the incoming date string and format it for the user's locale.

PBKDF2 iterations reduced 10x - weakens anonymity against brute-force attacks
## Issue

The anonymization system intentionally reduced PBKDF2 iterations for "speed":

- `generateAnonymousIdentity` in `lib/anonymization.ts:35`: reduced from 100,000 to 10,000 iterations
- Double hashing in `lib/supabase-auth.ts:72`: reduced from 50,000 to 5,000 iterations

## Why this matters

The anonymization system's security model depends on the PBKDF2 hash being computationally infeasible to brute-force. If an attacker obtains the database (which contains `verification_hash` and `salt`), they can attempt to reverse the hash by trying common email patterns:

- `student@iitbh.ac.in`
- `professor@iitbh.ac.in`
- Common name patterns at IIT Bhilai

At 10,000 iterations, this is **10x faster** to brute-force than the originally intended 100,000. Combined with the small email space (all IIT Bhilai students), a targeted attack could deanonymize users.

## Fix

1. Restore 100,000 iterations for `generateAnonymousIdentity`
2. Restore 50,000 iterations for the double-hash verification
3. If speed is a concern, consider client-server split: do the slow hash server-side only

XSS vulnerability: dangerouslySetInnerHTML in chart component
## 🔍 Issue

\`src/components/ui/chart.tsx:81\` uses \`dangerouslySetInnerHTML\` to render chart content.

### Context

This appears to be a custom chart component that renders HTML inside the chart labels/tooltips. If any chart data (labels, tooltips, axis values) comes from user input (e.g., course names, professor names, review text), malicious HTML could be injected.

### ✅ Fix

If this is a shadcn/ui or Radix chart component, the \`dangerouslySetInnerHTML\` is likely unnecessary. Check:

1. What data is being passed to the \`__html\` prop?
2. Can any of that data be user-controlled?
3. Switch to safe DOM text rendering or use DOMPurify if HTML rendering is required.

Additionally, \`scripts/scrape_professors.py:51\` uses \`requests.get(url, verify=False)\` — disabling SSL verification is dangerous and should be fixed in production.

\`src/components/ui/chart.tsx:81\` uses \`dangerouslySetInnerHTML\` to render chart content.

### Context

This appears to be a custom chart component that renders HTML inside the chart labels/tooltips. If any chart data (labels, tooltips, axis values) comes from user input (e.g., course names, professor names, review text), malicious HTML could be injected.

### ✅ Fix

If this is a shadcn/ui or Radix chart component, the \`dangerouslySetInnerHTML\` is likely unnecessary. Check:

1. What data is being passed to the \`__html\` prop?
2. Can any of that data be user-controlled?
3. Switch to safe DOM text rendering or use DOMPurify if HTML rendering is required.

Additionally, \`scripts/scrape_professors.py:51\` uses \`requests.get(url, verify=False)\` — disabling SSL verification is dangerous and should be fixed in production.

Add dark mode theme toggle with persistent preference
## Feature Request

### Problem
The app currently has no dark mode. Students doing lab work at night or preferring dark themes have no option.

### Proposed Solution
1. Dark/light theme toggle in the header
2. Persist preference via localStorage and in user profile
3. Respect `prefers-color-scheme` system preference as the default

### Technical Approach
- Add a `ThemeProvider` wrapping the entire app (Next.js already supports this pattern)
- CSS custom properties for colors, toggled on the `<html>` element's `data-theme` attribute
- The `PreferencesClient.js` component could be extended with a theme preference option
- The login/signup pages need separate theme handling (they don't use the main layout)

Add PDF export of complete lab reports including observations and calculations
## Feature Request

### Problem
Students currently manually take screenshots and compile lab reports. The experiments have structured data (observations tables, circuit diagrams, formulas in KaTeX, plots) that could be exported as a complete PDF.

### Proposed Solution
1. A "Export as PDF" button on each experiment page
2. PDF includes: experiment title, theory (with rendered KaTeX), circuit diagram, observation tables, calculations, and any generated plots
3. Styled PDF matching the standard IIT Bhilai lab report format

### Technical Approach
- Use pdfmake or @react-pdf/renderer for client-side PDF generation
- The experiment data is already structured in `sections` arrays with typed content blocks
- KaTeX rendering is already in use (`react-katex` dependency) — can render to SVG for PDF
- Plots are already Chart.js instances — `chart.toBase64Image()` for PDF embedding

Add offline-first support with IndexedDB caching for lab materials
## Feature Request

### Problem
Currently, lab content is fetched from the server/database on every page load. Students in areas with poor connectivity (or in labs with no internet) cannot access experiment instructions.

### Proposed Solution
1. Cache experiment data in IndexedDB via service worker
2. Serve cached content when offline
3. Show a "You are offline" badge
4. Background sync when connectivity is restored

### Technical Approach
- Use Workbox (already compatible with Next.js) for service worker management
- Cache experiment JSONs and images in IndexedDB
- The `fetchExperimentData()` server action could have an IndexedDB fallback
- The `generate_circuit_registry.js` script (in `/scripts/`) already creates local data bundles — these can be used as the offline cache seed

Login/signup form does not respond to Enter key (no onSubmit handler)
**Description**
The login/signup form at `app/login/page.js` has two handlers: `handleLogin` and `handleSignUp`, both triggered only via `onClick` on their respective buttons. The form itself has no `onSubmit` handler and no `action` attribute. Pressing Enter in the email or password fields triggers a browser default action (page reload/navigation) instead of submitting the form.

**Steps to Reproduce**
1. Go to `/login`
2. Type an email and password
3. Press the Enter key (inside an input field)
4. Observe that the page navigates instead of submitting

**Expected Behavior**
Pressing Enter in a form field should trigger the login/signup action (same as clicking the button).

**Root Cause**
`app/login/page.js` — The `<form>` element has:
- A login button: `type="submit" onClick={handleLogin}`
- A signup button: `type="button" onClick={handleSignUp}`
- No `onSubmit` handler on the `<form>` element itself

Race condition in job relevance scoring upvote/downvote endpoints
## Description

In `backend/controllers/jobs.controllers.js`, both `jobRelevanceScoreUpvote` and `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote` use a non-atomic read-modify-write pattern:

```js
const jobPosting = await JobPosting.findById(id);\n// ... check if already upvoted ...\njobPosting.upvotedBy.push(userId);\njobPosting.relevanceScore += 1;\nawait jobPosting.save();\n```

If two requests arrive concurrently for the same user voting on the same job, both reads see the user is not yet in `upvotedBy`, both push, and both increment the score. The user gets double-counted and the score becomes incorrect.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send two simultaneous POST requests to `/api/jobs/:id/upvote` with the same userId
2. Both requests pass the `includes` check before either saves
3. User appears twice in `upvotedBy` and score increments by 2

## Expected Behavior

Voting should be atomic — concurrent votes from the same user should only register once.

## Suggested Fix

Use MongoDB atomic operations with `findOneAndUpdate` and positional operators:

```js\nawait JobPosting.findOneAndUpdate(\n  { _id: id, upvotedBy: { $ne: userId } },\n  { $push: { upvotedBy: userId }, $inc: { relevanceScore: 1 } }\n);\n```

Or add a unique compound index on the parent array to prevent duplicates.

## Affected Files

- `backend/controllers/jobs.controllers.js` (upvote and downvote functions)

Referral system has no authentication or authorization — any unauthenticated user can create, view, and delete all referrals
## Description

The referral routes in `backend/routes/referral.routes.js` have no authentication middleware applied:

```js
router.post("/request", requestReferral);
router.post("/provide", provideReferral);
router.get("/", getReferrals);
router.delete("/:id", deleteReferral);
```

This means:
- **Any unauthenticated user** can create referral requests (leading to spam)
- **Any unauthenticated user** can view ALL referrals (exposing every student's name, email, resume link, and target company/job) — a serious PII leak
- **Any unauthenticated user** can delete ANY referral by ID

The `requestReferral`, `getReferrals`, and `deleteReferral` controllers use `req.body` or `req.params` without any check for who the current user is.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Without any auth token, send GET to `/api/referrals/` — returns all referrals with PII
2. Without any auth token, send DELETE to `/api/referrals/:id` — deletes any referral

## Expected Behavior

- `getReferrals` should require authentication and filter referrals based on user role (students see only their own, admins see all)
- `deleteReferral` should require authentication and verify ownership
- `provideReferral` should require authentication and verify the alumnus is providing their own link

## Suggested Fix

- Add `protectRoute` middleware to all referral routes
- Add ownership checks in controllers (compare referral's studentEmail/alumniEmail with `req.user.email`)
- Add role-based access (admin can view all, students view only theirs)

## Affected Files

- `backend/routes/referral.routes.js`
- `backend/controllers/referral.controller.js`

Verification token logged to console in production exposes account takeover vector
## Description

In `backend/controllers/auth.controller.js`, the signup controller logs the verification code to stdout:

```js
console.log("Generated verification code (signup):", verificationToken);
```

This means any production log aggregator (CloudWatch, Datadog, etc.) stores the 6-digit verification code in plaintext. Anyone with log access can verify any user's email and take over their account. The verification token is the sole factor for email verification — once verified, a JWT is issued.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Make a POST request to `/api/auth/signup` with a new user
2. Check server stdout logs
3. The verification code appears in plaintext

## Expected Behavior

Verification tokens should never be logged — only in development, and never in production.

## Suggested Fix

- Remove the `console.log` entirely, or gate it behind an env flag
- Consider adding rate limiting to `verifyEmail` and `sendCodeAgain` endpoints to prevent brute-force attacks on the 6-digit code space (1,000,000 possibilities is tractable without throttling)

## Affected Files

- `backend/controllers/auth.controller.js` (lines 70-71)

[Hacktoberfest] fix : Prevent Multiple Upvotes/Downvotes by Same Student.
### Description
Currently, the job relevance score (`jobRelevanceScoreUpvote` / `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote`)  
simply increments or decrements the score when called.  

This allows the same user to spam upvotes/downvotes multiple times.  

We need to **track user votes** and prevent repeated voting by the same user on the same job.

### Tasks
- [ ] Update the `JobPosting` model:
  - Add `upvotedBy: [ObjectId]` (array of user IDs).
  - Add `downvotedBy: [ObjectId]` (array of user IDs).
- [ ] Modify `jobRelevanceScoreUpvote`:
  - If user already upvoted → return error (`400 Already upvoted`).
  - If user previously downvoted → remove from `downvotedBy`, add to `upvotedBy`, and **increment score by 2** (switch vote).
  - Else → add user to `upvotedBy`, increment score by 1.
- [ ] Modify `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote` with similar logic.
- [ ] Ensure vote data is persisted correctly.
- [ ] Update API response to include whether the current user has upvoted/downvoted.

- [ ] Allow students to **edit the fields before submitting** if they want to override.

### Description
On the **Alumni Search page**, users can search alumni by specific criteria (e.g., name, Job, batch, company). However, once a search is performed, there is no way to return to the **default full alumni list** without manually refreshing the entire page.

This reduces usability and creates a frustrating user experience for students/alumni browsing the alumni database.

### Suggested Fix
- Add a **"Reset Search"** or **"Show All"** button next to the search bar.  
- When clicked, it should reload and display the **entire alumni list** without requiring a full page refresh.

Recruiter signup should accept any valid email address, without requiring an institute domain.  

**Actual Behavior:**  
The form validation requires an institute email, blocking recruiters who use general or company email addresses.

[Hacktoberfest] Job Application Save Button Does Not Reflect Saved State
**Issue:**  
Clicking the "Save" button on a job application always triggers the "Application saved" popup, even if the application is already in the saved list.  
The button never changes to indicate that the job is already saved, leading to repeated saves.

**Steps to Reproduce:**  
1. Go to the Job Applications page.  
2. Click "Save" on any job application.  
3. Notice the "Application saved" popup appears.  
4. Click the same "Save" button again — the popup appears again instead of showing it’s already saved.  

**Expected Behavior:**  
After saving a job application, the button should change to "Saved" (or "Unsave") and prevent repeated save actions unless the user explicitly unsaves it.  

**Actual Behavior:**  
The button remains in the "Save" state and always triggers the save popup on click, regardless of whether the application is already saved.

issue_2_text:
Race condition in job relevance scoring upvote/downvote endpoints
## Description

In `backend/controllers/jobs.controllers.js`, both `jobRelevanceScoreUpvote` and `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote` use a non-atomic read-modify-write pattern:

```js
const jobPosting = await JobPosting.findById(id);\n// ... check if already upvoted ...\njobPosting.upvotedBy.push(userId);\njobPosting.relevanceScore += 1;\nawait jobPosting.save();\n```

If two requests arrive concurrently for the same user voting on the same job, both reads see the user is not yet in `upvotedBy`, both push, and both increment the score. The user gets double-counted and the score becomes incorrect.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send two simultaneous POST requests to `/api/jobs/:id/upvote` with the same userId
2. Both requests pass the `includes` check before either saves
3. User appears twice in `upvotedBy` and score increments by 2

## Expected Behavior

Voting should be atomic — concurrent votes from the same user should only register once.

## Suggested Fix

Use MongoDB atomic operations with `findOneAndUpdate` and positional operators:

```js\nawait JobPosting.findOneAndUpdate(\n  { _id: id, upvotedBy: { $ne: userId } },\n  { $push: { upvotedBy: userId }, $inc: { relevanceScore: 1 } }\n);\n```

Or add a unique compound index on the parent array to prevent duplicates.

## Affected Files

- `backend/controllers/jobs.controllers.js` (upvote and downvote functions)

issue_2_text:
Referral system has no authentication or authorization — any unauthenticated user can create, view, and delete all referrals
## Description

The referral routes in `backend/routes/referral.routes.js` have no authentication middleware applied:

```js
router.post("/request", requestReferral);
router.post("/provide", provideReferral);
router.get("/", getReferrals);
router.delete("/:id", deleteReferral);
```

This means:
- **Any unauthenticated user** can create referral requests (leading to spam)
- **Any unauthenticated user** can view ALL referrals (exposing every student's name, email, resume link, and target company/job) — a serious PII leak
- **Any unauthenticated user** can delete ANY referral by ID

The `requestReferral`, `getReferrals`, and `deleteReferral` controllers use `req.body` or `req.params` without any check for who the current user is.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Without any auth token, send GET to `/api/referrals/` — returns all referrals with PII
2. Without any auth token, send DELETE to `/api/referrals/:id` — deletes any referral

## Expected Behavior

- `getReferrals` should require authentication and filter referrals based on user role (students see only their own, admins see all)
- `deleteReferral` should require authentication and verify ownership
- `provideReferral` should require authentication and verify the alumnus is providing their own link

## Suggested Fix

- Add `protectRoute` middleware to all referral routes
- Add ownership checks in controllers (compare referral's studentEmail/alumniEmail with `req.user.email`)
- Add role-based access (admin can view all, students view only theirs)

## Affected Files

- `backend/routes/referral.routes.js`
- `backend/controllers/referral.controller.js`

issue_2_text:
Verification token logged to console in production exposes account takeover vector
## Description

In `backend/controllers/auth.controller.js`, the signup controller logs the verification code to stdout:

```js
console.log("Generated verification code (signup):", verificationToken);
```

This means any production log aggregator (CloudWatch, Datadog, etc.) stores the 6-digit verification code in plaintext. Anyone with log access can verify any user's email and take over their account. The verification token is the sole factor for email verification — once verified, a JWT is issued.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Make a POST request to `/api/auth/signup` with a new user
2. Check server stdout logs
3. The verification code appears in plaintext

## Expected Behavior

Verification tokens should never be logged — only in development, and never in production.

## Suggested Fix

- Remove the `console.log` entirely, or gate it behind an env flag
- Consider adding rate limiting to `verifyEmail` and `sendCodeAgain` endpoints to prevent brute-force attacks on the 6-digit code space (1,000,000 possibilities is tractable without throttling)

## Affected Files

- `backend/controllers/auth.controller.js` (lines 70-71)

### Description
Currently, the job relevance score (`jobRelevanceScoreUpvote` / `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote`)

  - If user previously downvoted → remove from `downvotedBy`, add to `upvotedBy`, and **increment score by 2** (switch vote).
  - Else → add user to `upvotedBy`, increment score by 1.
- [ ] Modify `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote` with similar logic.
- [ ] Ensure vote data is persisted correctly.
- [ ] Update API response to include whether the current user has upvoted/downvoted.

issue_1_text:
Race condition in job relevance scoring upvote/downvote endpoints
## Description

In `backend/controllers/jobs.controllers.js`, both `jobRelevanceScoreUpvote` and `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote` use a non-atomic read-modify-write pattern:

```js
const jobPosting = await JobPosting.findById(id);\n// ... check if already upvoted ...\njobPosting.upvotedBy.push(userId);\njobPosting.relevanceScore += 1;\nawait jobPosting.save();\n```

If two requests arrive concurrently for the same user voting on the same job, both reads see the user is not yet in `upvotedBy`, both push, and both increment the score. The user gets double-counted and the score becomes incorrect.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send two simultaneous POST requests to `/api/jobs/:id/upvote` with the same userId
2. Both requests pass the `includes` check before either saves
3. User appears twice in `upvotedBy` and score increments by 2

## Expected Behavior

Voting should be atomic — concurrent votes from the same user should only register once.

## Suggested Fix

Use MongoDB atomic operations with `findOneAndUpdate` and positional operators:

```js\nawait JobPosting.findOneAndUpdate(\n  { _id: id, upvotedBy: { $ne: userId } },\n  { $push: { upvotedBy: userId }, $inc: { relevanceScore: 1 } }\n);\n```

Or add a unique compound index on the parent array to prevent duplicates.

## Affected Files

- `backend/controllers/jobs.controllers.js` (upvote and downvote functions)

issue_2_text:
Referral system has no authentication or authorization — any unauthenticated user can create, view, and delete all referrals
## Description

The referral routes in `backend/routes/referral.routes.js` have no authentication middleware applied:

```js
router.post("/request", requestReferral);
router.post("/provide", provideReferral);
router.get("/", getReferrals);
router.delete("/:id", deleteReferral);
```

This means:
- **Any unauthenticated user** can create referral requests (leading to spam)
- **Any unauthenticated user** can view ALL referrals (exposing every student's name, email, resume link, and target company/job) — a serious PII leak
- **Any unauthenticated user** can delete ANY referral by ID

The `requestReferral`, `getReferrals`, and `deleteReferral` controllers use `req.body` or `req.params` without any check for who the current user is.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Without any auth token, send GET to `/api/referrals/` — returns all referrals with PII
2. Without any auth token, send DELETE to `/api/referrals/:id` — deletes any referral

## Expected Behavior

- `getReferrals` should require authentication and filter referrals based on user role (students see only their own, admins see all)
- `deleteReferral` should require authentication and verify ownership
- `provideReferral` should require authentication and verify the alumnus is providing their own link

## Suggested Fix

- Add `protectRoute` middleware to all referral routes
- Add ownership checks in controllers (compare referral's studentEmail/alumniEmail with `req.user.email`)
- Add role-based access (admin can view all, students view only theirs)

## Affected Files

- `backend/routes/referral.routes.js`
- `backend/controllers/referral.controller.js`

issue_2_text:
Verification token logged to console in production exposes account takeover vector
## Description

In `backend/controllers/auth.controller.js`, the signup controller logs the verification code to stdout:

```js
console.log("Generated verification code (signup):", verificationToken);
```

This means any production log aggregator (CloudWatch, Datadog, etc.) stores the 6-digit verification code in plaintext. Anyone with log access can verify any user's email and take over their account. The verification token is the sole factor for email verification — once verified, a JWT is issued.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Make a POST request to `/api/auth/signup` with a new user
2. Check server stdout logs
3. The verification code appears in plaintext

## Expected Behavior

Verification tokens should never be logged — only in development, and never in production.

## Suggested Fix

- Remove the `console.log` entirely, or gate it behind an env flag
- Consider adding rate limiting to `verifyEmail` and `sendCodeAgain` endpoints to prevent brute-force attacks on the 6-digit code space (1,000,000 possibilities is tractable without throttling)

## Affected Files

- `backend/controllers/auth.controller.js` (lines 70-71)

Currently, the job relevance score (`jobRelevanceScoreUpvote` / `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote`)

We need to **track user votes** and prevent repeated voting by the same user on the same job.

- [ ] Update the `JobPosting` model:

  - Else → add user to `upvotedBy`, increment score by 1.
- [ ] Modify `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote` with similar logic.
- [ ] Ensure vote data is persisted correctly.
- [ ] Update API response to include whether the current user has upvoted/downvoted.

Race condition in job relevance scoring upvote/downvote endpoints
## Description

In `backend/controllers/jobs.controllers.js`, both `jobRelevanceScoreUpvote` and `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote` use a non-atomic read-modify-write pattern:

```js
const jobPosting = await JobPosting.findById(id);\n// ... check if already upvoted ...\njobPosting.upvotedBy.push(userId);\njobPosting.relevanceScore += 1;\nawait jobPosting.save();\n```

If two requests arrive concurrently for the same user voting on the same job, both reads see the user is not yet in `upvotedBy`, both push, and both increment the score. The user gets double-counted and the score becomes incorrect.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send two simultaneous POST requests to `/api/jobs/:id/upvote` with the same userId
2. Both requests pass the `includes` check before either saves
3. User appears twice in `upvotedBy` and score increments by 2

## Expected Behavior

Voting should be atomic — concurrent votes from the same user should only register once.

## Suggested Fix

Use MongoDB atomic operations with `findOneAndUpdate` and positional operators:

```js\nawait JobPosting.findOneAndUpdate(\n  { _id: id, upvotedBy: { $ne: userId } },\n  { $push: { upvotedBy: userId }, $inc: { relevanceScore: 1 } }\n);\n```

Or add a unique compound index on the parent array to prevent duplicates.

## Affected Files

- `backend/controllers/jobs.controllers.js` (upvote and downvote functions)

issue_1_text:
Race condition in job relevance scoring upvote/downvote endpoints
## Description

In `backend/controllers/jobs.controllers.js`, both `jobRelevanceScoreUpvote` and `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote` use a non-atomic read-modify-write pattern:

```js
const jobPosting = await JobPosting.findById(id);\n// ... check if already upvoted ...\njobPosting.upvotedBy.push(userId);\njobPosting.relevanceScore += 1;\nawait jobPosting.save();\n```

If two requests arrive concurrently for the same user voting on the same job, both reads see the user is not yet in `upvotedBy`, both push, and both increment the score. The user gets double-counted and the score becomes incorrect.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send two simultaneous POST requests to `/api/jobs/:id/upvote` with the same userId
2. Both requests pass the `includes` check before either saves
3. User appears twice in `upvotedBy` and score increments by 2

## Expected Behavior

Voting should be atomic — concurrent votes from the same user should only register once.

## Suggested Fix

Use MongoDB atomic operations with `findOneAndUpdate` and positional operators:

```js\nawait JobPosting.findOneAndUpdate(\n  { _id: id, upvotedBy: { $ne: userId } },\n  { $push: { upvotedBy: userId }, $inc: { relevanceScore: 1 } }\n);\n```

Or add a unique compound index on the parent array to prevent duplicates.

## Affected Files

- `backend/controllers/jobs.controllers.js` (upvote and downvote functions)

issue_2_text:
Referral system has no authentication or authorization — any unauthenticated user can create, view, and delete all referrals
## Description

The referral routes in `backend/routes/referral.routes.js` have no authentication middleware applied:

```js
router.post("/request", requestReferral);
router.post("/provide", provideReferral);
router.get("/", getReferrals);
router.delete("/:id", deleteReferral);
```

This means:
- **Any unauthenticated user** can create referral requests (leading to spam)
- **Any unauthenticated user** can view ALL referrals (exposing every student's name, email, resume link, and target company/job) — a serious PII leak
- **Any unauthenticated user** can delete ANY referral by ID

The `requestReferral`, `getReferrals`, and `deleteReferral` controllers use `req.body` or `req.params` without any check for who the current user is.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Without any auth token, send GET to `/api/referrals/` — returns all referrals with PII
2. Without any auth token, send DELETE to `/api/referrals/:id` — deletes any referral

## Expected Behavior

- `getReferrals` should require authentication and filter referrals based on user role (students see only their own, admins see all)
- `deleteReferral` should require authentication and verify ownership
- `provideReferral` should require authentication and verify the alumnus is providing their own link

## Suggested Fix

- Add `protectRoute` middleware to all referral routes
- Add ownership checks in controllers (compare referral's studentEmail/alumniEmail with `req.user.email`)
- Add role-based access (admin can view all, students view only theirs)

## Affected Files

- `backend/routes/referral.routes.js`
- `backend/controllers/referral.controller.js`

issue_2_text:
Verification token logged to console in production exposes account takeover vector
## Description

In `backend/controllers/auth.controller.js`, the signup controller logs the verification code to stdout:

```js
console.log("Generated verification code (signup):", verificationToken);
```

This means any production log aggregator (CloudWatch, Datadog, etc.) stores the 6-digit verification code in plaintext. Anyone with log access can verify any user's email and take over their account. The verification token is the sole factor for email verification — once verified, a JWT is issued.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Make a POST request to `/api/auth/signup` with a new user
2. Check server stdout logs
3. The verification code appears in plaintext

## Expected Behavior

Verification tokens should never be logged — only in development, and never in production.

## Suggested Fix

- Remove the `console.log` entirely, or gate it behind an env flag
- Consider adding rate limiting to `verifyEmail` and `sendCodeAgain` endpoints to prevent brute-force attacks on the 6-digit code space (1,000,000 possibilities is tractable without throttling)

## Affected Files

- `backend/controllers/auth.controller.js` (lines 70-71)

Add notification system for application status changes and job deadline reminders
## Description

Currently the platform has no internal notification system. Students applying to jobs have no way of receiving in-app notifications when:
- Their application status changes (shortlisted, rejected, accepted)
- A saved job's deadline is approaching
- A new job matching their skills/profile is posted

## Proposed Feature

Implement a notification system with:
1. **Backend**: Notification model, REST endpoints for CRUD, and a scheduled job that checks upcoming deadlines (e.g., 48h before expiry)
2. **Frontend**: Notification bell component with unread count badge, notification dropdown, and mark-as-read functionality
3. **Real-time**: Optionally integrate WebSocket/Socket.io for push notifications

## Additional Context

- The email infrastructure already exists in `backend/config/nodemailer.js` and `backend/utils/emails.js`
- Notifications could be stored in MongoDB with fields: `userId`, `type`, `message`, `isRead`, `createdAt`, `relatedJobId`
- Could leverage existing scheduled jobs pattern for deadline reminders

[Hacktoberfest] Improve JWT handling: auto-clear expired tokens from localStorage
###Current Behavior
- After login, the JWT is returned in the response and stored in `localStorage`.
- When the token expires, the app continues trying to use it.
- This results in login failures until the user manually clears `localStorage`.

###Expected Behavior
- The frontend should automatically detect expired tokens in `localStorage`.
- Expired tokens should be removed from storage without requiring manual intervention.
- When no valid token is present, the user should be redirected to the login screen.

[Hacktoberfest] fix : Prevent Multiple Upvotes/Downvotes by Same Student.
### Description
Currently, the job relevance score (`jobRelevanceScoreUpvote` / `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote`)  
simply increments or decrements the score when called.  

This allows the same user to spam upvotes/downvotes multiple times.  

We need to **track user votes** and prevent repeated voting by the same user on the same job.

### Tasks
- [ ] Update the `JobPosting` model:
  - Add `upvotedBy: [ObjectId]` (array of user IDs).
  - Add `downvotedBy: [ObjectId]` (array of user IDs).
- [ ] Modify `jobRelevanceScoreUpvote`:
  - If user already upvoted → return error (`400 Already upvoted`).
  - If user previously downvoted → remove from `downvotedBy`, add to `upvotedBy`, and **increment score by 2** (switch vote).
  - Else → add user to `upvotedBy`, increment score by 1.
- [ ] Modify `jobRelevanceScoreDownvote` with similar logic.
- [ ] Ensure vote data is persisted correctly.
- [ ] Update API response to include whether the current user has upvoted/downvoted.

### Description
On the **Alumni Search page**, users can search alumni by specific criteria (e.g., name, Job, batch, company). However, once a search is performed, there is no way to return to the **default full alumni list** without manually refreshing the entire page.

2. Enter a search term .

4. Try to return to the default full list.

There should be a **"Reset Search"** or **"Show All"** button that clears the current search and reloads the complete alumni list.

### Actual Behavior
Currently, users must refresh the page to reset the search and view the full list again.

### Impact
This reduces usability and creates a frustrating user experience for students/alumni browsing the alumni database.

### Suggested Fix
- Add a **"Reset Search"** or **"Show All"** button next to the search bar.  
- When clicked, it should reload and display the **entire alumni list** without requiring a full page refresh.

[Hacktoberfest] Recruiter Signup Requires Institute Email Instead of Accepting All Emails
**Issue:**  
During recruiter signup, the email field is incorrectly restricted to institute email addresses (i.e., ending with .@ittbhilai.ac.in).  
Recruiters often do not have institute emails, so this validation prevents legitimate recruiter accounts from being created.

4. The form rejects the email as invalid.

**Expected Behavior:**  
Recruiter signup should accept any valid email address, without requiring an institute domain.  

**Actual Behavior:**  
The form validation requires an institute email, blocking recruiters who use general or company email addresses.

[Hacktoberfest] Job Application Save Button Does Not Reflect Saved State
**Issue:**  
Clicking the "Save" button on a job application always triggers the "Application saved" popup, even if the application is already in the saved list.  
The button never changes to indicate that the job is already saved, leading to repeated saves.

**Steps to Reproduce:**  
1. Go to the Job Applications page.  
2. Click "Save" on any job application.  
3. Notice the "Application saved" popup appears.  
4. Click the same "Save" button again — the popup appears again instead of showing it’s already saved.  

**Expected Behavior:**  
After saving a job application, the button should change to "Saved" (or "Unsave") and prevent repeated save actions unless the user explicitly unsaves it.  

**Actual Behavior:**  
The button remains in the "Save" state and always triggers the save popup on click, regardless of whether the application is already saved.
